title: Platform detected
question: Which platform serves the store?
method: Informational. Recognise the platform from home page fingerprints (and, on a WordPress site with product pages, from the first sampled product page, which can reveal WooCommerce), first match wins, in this order: WooCommerce, Shopify, BigCommerce, Adobe Commerce (Magento), Shopware, PrestaShop, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Square Online, Ecwid, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, WordPress (generator tags, body classes, asset hosts, asset paths and response headers). Always passes when it runs, with the platform, the matching fingerprint and the generator tag as evidence. The result selects the profile, the platform-specific checks and the platform notes of fixes. It is never scored and gates no level.

title: Store API reachable
question: Can an agent read products through the Store API without credentials?
method: WooCommerce only. GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1 without credentials. Pass on HTTP 200 with a JSON array (an empty array included), recording the X-WP-Total header. Skipped as inconclusive on 429, 502, 503, 504 or no response. Fail on 401 or 403 (authentication required), on any other status including 404, on a non-JSON body, or on JSON that is not an array.

title: Store API product completeness
question: Do Store API products carry the fields an agent needs?
method: WooCommerce only. Read up to 20 products from /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=20. Skipped as inconclusive when the list answers 429, 502, 503 or 504 or does not answer. Fail when the list is not HTTP 200 with a JSON array, when it is empty, or when any product lacks name, permalink (an entry without both as text is counted as incomplete), prices.price, prices.currency_code or a true or false is_in_stock. Warn when those are present but some products have no images or no categories. Pass when every product carries all seven fields.

title: Public product feed discoverable
question: Can an agent reach the catalog as a feed without an account?
method: Collect feed candidates in this order: rel=alternate link tags of the home page with an RSS, Atom, XML or JSON type (those whose URL or title mentions product, feed, merchant, Google or shopping, else a single RSS or Atom link), llms.txt links that suggest a feed, robots.txt Sitemap and comment lines with a URL that contains "feed", and sitemap entries that are feed paths or data files (never a product page whose slug contains the word). Fetch up to the first two. Pass on HTTP 200 with a Google-format XML feed (the g: namespace, or items with g:id or g:price), a CSV or TSV whose header has id, title, link (or url) and price, JSON or JSON Lines items with those fields, or an OpenAI-format feed (CSV, TSV, JSON or JSON Lines with item_id or sku, title, url or link, and price), which is recorded as such. Fail when no candidate is found or none of those tried is a product feed. Every shopping surface ingests feeds pushed through its own channel and none documents reading a merchant-hosted URL, so a public copy is a convenience for agents, not a requirement: weight 1. The specifications are cited for the formats only.

title: Feed freshness
question: Was the feed updated recently?
method: Skipped unless B1.5 found a feed. Fetch it again and read the Last-Modified header and a timestamp inside the feed (lastBuildDate or pubDate in RSS, updated in Atom, a top-level updated_at, generated_at, last_updated or updated in JSON, else the first item's pubDate or updated). Measure the newer one against the response's Date header. Pass within 24 hours, warn within 7 days, fail beyond, and fail when the feed is no longer HTTP 200 or carries no parseable timestamp. The thresholds are this scanner's heuristic, as no channel publishes one.

title: Catalog in sitemap matches Store API
question: Do the sitemap and the Store API agree on catalog size?
method: WooCommerce only. Compare the product URL count in the sitemap with the X-WP-Total header of /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1. The deviation is the difference divided by the larger count. Pass within 10 percent, warn within 25 percent, fail beyond, and fail when the header is missing or not a number or either count is zero. Skipped as inconclusive when the Store API answers 429, 502, 503 or 504 or does not answer, and skipped when there is no sitemap or not every product sitemap was read within the request budget.

title: Shopify products.json readable
question: Can an agent read a Shopify catalog as JSON?
method: Shopify only. GET /products.json?limit=5. Pass on HTTP 200 with JSON that holds a products array. Skipped as inconclusive on no response and on a gateway error (502, 503, 504). Fail on 401, 404, the storefront password page, any HTML page, any other non-200 status, a non-JSON body or JSON without a products array. Warn when the store's robots.txt disallows the URL for the scanner, so it was not requested. Skipped on 429, because Shopify rate-limits this endpoint per IP after a few requests. A headless storefront, which loads Shopify assets but lacks the response headers Shopify's own servers send, is skipped as not applicable: Shopify serves neither products.json nor the UCP endpoint on that domain. The endpoint is an undocumented but long-standing convention of every Online Store theme (the documented per-product form is /products/<handle>.js). Shopify's generated robots.txt and agents.md now point agents at the UCP catalog on /api/ucp/mcp instead, which B5.8 covers, so this check carries weight 2 and B5.8 counts as a readable catalog for Level 2.

title: Adobe Commerce catalog over GraphQL
question: Can an agent query the Magento catalog over GraphQL without a token?
method: Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source only. Send one read-only catalog query to /graphql with GET, as Adobe documents for queries (products with search "a", one item, name, SKU and URL key). Pass on HTTP 200 with data.products.items and no errors. Warn when the answer carries GraphQL errors, with or without products, or when robots.txt keeps the scanner from asking. Fail on 401 or 403 without a GraphQL answer, on an HTML page (a firewall rule or redirect in front of /graphql), on 404 or on any other answer that is not GraphQL. Skipped on 429, a gateway error (502, 503, 504) or no response. Anonymous REST access stays off by default and is not tested.
